title: Trust in Allah, but Calculation Too • Ten Years, One Call • The Fire of Bu‘ath • Six, Then Twelve • Madinah’s First Teacher • Seventy-Three • The Terms of the Night of ‘Aqabah • The Shout of Shaytan • The Pursuit After ‘Aqabah • Hijrah, One by One • Umm Salamah’s Lone Journey

blocks.0: Trust in Allah, but Calculation Too
blocks.1: The season of Hajj. Rows of tents at Mina. A man is walking among the tents. This very man has travelled through the seven heavens. At Sidrat al-Muntaha he was summoned. Fifty to five. And coming down in the morning, he saw that Makkah was just as it had been.
blocks.2: The three-year siege had passed. Abu Talib was gone, Khadijah (RA) was gone. He had to return from Ta’if struck by stones.{{1}}
blocks.3: Yet he did not stop. The message of Allah is not a thing that stops. It must be delivered. And to deliver it, one needs a land where people will listen, and where one can stay safe with faith.
blocks.4: Today’s dars is the story of searching for that land; of searching for a home. A pledge in the dark of night in the mountain pass of ‘Aqabah. Then a night’s farewell, leaving Makkah. The cave on Mount Thawr. And finally, in a city of date orchards, a she-camel coming to a halt.
blocks.5: The reckoning of time is from the mouth of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA).
blocks.7: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} was sent (as a prophet) at the age of forty. After that he stayed in Makkah for thirteen years; revelation came to him. Then he was commanded to make the Hijrah.{{2}}
blocks.8: Today is the story of the final chapter of those thirteen years. One question will be with us through the whole story. Did the Prophet {{1}} sit relying only on Allah? Or at every step did he also calculate along with his trust?
blocks.9: And in our own work, how much is trust, and how much is calculation?
blocks.11: That search for a home the Prophet {{1}} did at market after market, fair after fair. At ‘Ukaz, at Majinnah, and in the Hajj season at Mina. Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA) has told of those days. He himself is a man of Yathrib; a man right at the heart of the events.
blocks.13: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} stayed in Makkah ten years. Going to the people’s camping places, at ‘Ukaz and Majinnah and in the Hajj season at Mina, he would say, who will give me shelter? Who will help me, so that I may deliver the message of my Lord; and for that person, Paradise.{{2}}
blocks.16: It even happened that someone would come from Yemen or Egypt (the narrator said it so); his people would come and say, beware of the boy of Quraysh, lest he put you into trial. He would walk among their tents, and they would point at him with their fingers.{{1}}
blocks.17: Then one day the answer to that call came. It came from where no one expected.
blocks.19: Yathrib was then a weary city. Aws and Khazraj; two tribes of the same city. Long enmity. Blood for blood. And the most terrible of those wars was named Bu‘ath.{{1}}
blocks.20: ‘A’ishah (RA) has told of that day in one sentence.
blocks.22: The day of Bu‘ath was a day Allah had brought forward (in advance) for His Messenger. When the Messenger of Allah {{1}} came (to Madinah), their ranks had broken, their chiefs were killed, and many were wounded. In this way, concerning their entry into Islam, Allah had brought that day forward for His Messenger.{{2}}
blocks.23: A city had been shattered by war. In that shattered city, one day, a man was needed who could hold everyone together. Allah had made the very time of breaking into the preparation before the coming of His Prophet.
blocks.25: In one Hajj season the Prophet {{1}} met six men at Mina. All were of the Khazraj tribe. He spoke with them, called them to Allah. In Yathrib their neighbours were the Jews. Whenever a quarrel broke out, the Jews would say, the time of a prophet is near; we will go with him and kill you the way ‘Ad and Iram were killed. The six turned to one another and said, by Allah, this is the very prophet the Jews name to frighten us. Let them not reach him before us.{{2}}
blocks.26: They believed. And before leaving they said, our tribe is broken by war; there is no enmity like it in any other tribe. Perhaps Allah will join us together through you. We will go back and call them. If Allah gathers them around you, no one will be more honoured than you.
blocks.27: The six went back. The next Hajj, twelve came; ten of the Khazraj, two of the Aws. At the pass of ‘Aqabah they pledged at the hand of the Prophet {{1}}. This is the first ‘Aqabah.{{2}}
blocks.28: The terms of that pledge ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA) has told in his own words.
blocks.30: I am one of those naqibs who pledged to the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. We pledged on this: that we would not associate anything with Allah, would not steal, would not commit adultery, would not kill the soul Allah has made sacred, would not plunder, would not disobey; in return, Paradise, if we fulfilled these. And if we fell into any of these, the decision about it is in Allah’s hands.{{2}}
blocks.31: One thing needs to be clear here. In this narration of Bukhari it is not written which night of ‘Aqabah it is about. Ibn Ishaq called it the terms of the first ‘Aqabah; that part is from the Sirah, not in the main text of the hadith. The aim was one: tawhid and character. War had not yet come up.
blocks.33: As the twelve returned they left a request. Send with us someone who will teach us our din.{{1}}
blocks.34: The Prophet {{1}} sent Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA). A strange city. In hand only the Qur’an. What happened afterwards in house after house of Yathrib, Jabir (RA) has told himself.
blocks.36: At last Allah sent us from Yathrib to him. We gave him shelter, we affirmed him as true. One of us would go out, believe in him, and he would make him recite the Qur’an; he would return to his people, and they too would become Muslims through his Islam. In the end there remained no house among the Ansar in which a group of Muslims was not openly showing Islam.{{1}}
blocks.37: What was not found in ten years going door to door, Allah gave from a place whose name was then in no one’s calculation. No army, no sword; one teacher, and the Qur’an.
blocks.38: After faith came, the Muslims of Yathrib sat among themselves. A question on their lips.
blocks.40: We said, how long shall we leave the Messenger of Allah {{1}} like this? He is being chased from mountain to mountain of Makkah, and he lives in fear.{{2}}
blocks.41: That question they answered themselves; a caravan, on the road to Makkah.
blocks.43: The next Hajj. A caravan came from Yathrib to Makkah. In the caravan there were polytheists and Muslims. The Muslims kept their faith hidden. Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA) said, we were keeping the matter secret from the polytheists with us.{{1}}
blocks.44: They also decided not to leave without one man. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA); their chief. They said to him, you are one of our chiefs, one of our notable men. We cannot accept that tomorrow you will be fuel for Hell. He accepted Islam. He was present that night at ‘Aqabah. Later he also became a naqib (leader).{{1}}
blocks.45: When a third of the night had passed, they rose from their beds. Unknown to everyone. In the words of Ka‘b (RA), as quietly and stealthily as sandgrouse. Seventy-three men gathered in the pass. With them two women; Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA), whose kunyah is Umm ‘Umarah, and Asma’ bint ‘Amr (RA), who is also called Umm Mani‘.{{1}}
blocks.46: Another person also came to the pass whom no one had expected. The Prophet {{1}} came to the pass, with his uncle ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib. He was still in the religion of his tribe. But he wanted to see his nephew’s affair with his own eyes, to be certain. ‘Abbas spoke first of all. He said, O people of the Khazraj! You know what Muhammad is among us. Even from those who think as we do, we have protected him. He is honoured among his own tribe, safe in his own city. Yet he wishes to go to you. If you think you can keep the call by which you called him and protect him from his opponents, then take your responsibility. And if you think you will take him and abandon him, then stop right now.{{2}}
blocks.47: In reply they said, we have heard your words. O Messenger of Allah, now you speak. Take from us what you wish, for yourself and for your Lord.
blocks.48: The Terms of the Night of ‘Aqabah
blocks.49: The Prophet {{1}} recited the Qur’an. He called to Allah. Then he stated the terms. Jabir (RA) has kept the sentences of the terms by heart.
blocks.51: You will pledge to me to listen and obey, in times of eagerness and in times of laziness; to spend, in ease and in hardship; to command good and forbid evil; to speak for Allah, fearing no blame of any blamer in the matter of Allah; and when I come to you, you will help me and protect me as you protect yourselves, your wives and your children. And for you, Paradise.{{1}}
blocks.52: They stood up. They stretched out their hands. But before the hands touched, one stopped them. As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA); one of the youngest of the group.
blocks.54: Wait, people of Yathrib! We have driven our camels this far only because we know that this is the Messenger of Allah. To take him out today means to cut ties with all of Arabia, to see the best of you killed, and to be bitten by swords. If you can bear all this, take him; your reward is with Allah. And if you fear cowardice within yourselves, leave him now; with Allah that is the more acceptable excuse for you. They said, step aside, As‘ad (RA)! By Allah, we will never give up this pledge, never take it back.{{1}}
blocks.55: The smallest man said the most careful word. Then al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur (RA) took the hand of the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.57: Yes, by Him who sent you with the truth, we will protect you from whatever we protect our izar (that is, our families) from. Take our pledge, O Messenger of Allah! We are children of war, men of arms; we have inherited this from our elders.{{1}}
blocks.58: In the midst of the talk another man cut in. Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA). A fear was in his mind. We are cutting all the old treaties with the Jews. If Allah gives you victory, will you go back to your own people and leave us? The Prophet {{1}} smiled. Then he said, blood is my blood, destruction is my destruction. I am yours, you are mine. Whoever you fight, I will fight; whoever you make peace with, I will make peace with.{{2}}
blocks.59: Then the matter of the naqibs.
blocks.61: Bring out to me twelve naqibs from among you, who will be in charge of their respective tribes. They brought out twelve naqibs; nine of the Khazraj, three of the Aws.{{1}}
blocks.62: Among the nine of the Khazraj were As‘ad ibn Zurarah, Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur, ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit, ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA). Among the three of the Aws was Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA).{{1}}
blocks.63: A small point; after ten years of rejection, those who came and stood beside the Prophet {{1}} were also willing to take responsibility for their own tribes. The pledge was not only in emotion; it was in structure too.
blocks.65: The pledge ended. Just then a shout rose from the top of ‘Aqabah.
blocks.67: When we finished the pledge, Shaytan shouted from the top of ‘Aqabah in a voice so far-reaching that I had never heard the like; O people of the camps! Have you nothing to do about Mudhammam and the apostates with him? (Ibn Ishaq explained: the enemy of Allah meant Muhammad by this.) They have agreed to war against you! The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, this is the ‘Azab of ‘Aqabah, the son of Azyab (that is, Shaytan). Listen, enemy of Allah! By Allah, I will surely make time for you. Then the Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, go back to your tents. ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) said, by Him who sent you with the truth, if you wish, tomorrow we will fall upon the people of Mina with our swords. The Messenger of Allah {{3}} said, I have not been commanded to do this.{{4}}
blocks.68: At dawn the elders of Quraysh arrived. Right at the tents of the Yathrib caravan, one after another. They said, O people of the Khazraj! We have heard that you came to our companion. You want to take him out from among us, and you pledged at his hand for war against us. By Allah, there is no tribe among the Arabs with whom a war breaking out with us is more disliked by us than with you. Then the polytheists of the caravan swore by Allah and said, nothing like this happened, we know nothing. And they spoke the truth; they truly did not know. The Muslims kept looking at one another’s faces.{{1}}
blocks.69: The Quraysh group was getting up to leave. Among them a youth of the Makhzum tribe, with shiny new shoes on his feet. Ka‘b (RA) said in passing, Abu Jabir, can you not get a pair of shoes like this Qurayshi youth? Hearing it, the youth took off his shoes and threw them at him. He said, by Allah, you will wear these. In a night full of fear there was such a small light moment too.{{1}}
blocks.71: Quraysh went back, but suspicion did not. They went to ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul; the greatest chief of the Khazraj. They said the same thing: your people have reportedly pledged for war with our companion. He said, this is a great matter. My tribe would not do this without informing me; I know nothing. They went back.{{1}}
blocks.72: Mina began to empty. Quraysh enquired and learned the event was true. They set out after the caravan. Two naqibs were caught; Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) and Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA). Mundhir broke away and escaped. They caught Sa‘d (RA). They tied his hand to his neck with the camel’s rope. Beating him, dragging him by the hair, they brought him into Makkah.
blocks.73: While I was in their hands, some of the Quraysh came. Among them a fair, handsome man. I said to myself, if any of these has anything good, it will be with this one. He came close, raised his hand, and punched me hard. Then I knew that these have nothing good left.{{1}}
blocks.74: Then one of them said, do you not have a security pact with anyone of Quraysh? Sa‘d (RA) said, I do. I used to give security to the trade caravan of Jubayr ibn Mut‘im in my area, so that no one would wrong them. And the caravan of al-Harith ibn Harb too. The man said, then call out the names of those two. He called. Those two were sitting in the mosque beside the Ka‘bah then. Hearing the news they said, he speaks the truth; he used to give our traders security and did not let wrong be done to them. They came and freed Sa‘d (RA).{{1}}
blocks.76: Allah showed the Prophet {{1}} the home. In a dream. In the narration of Suhayb (RA) the Prophet {{2}} had said it was either Hajar or Yathrib.{{3}}
blocks.78: The Prophet {{1}} was then in Makkah. He said to the Muslims, I have been shown the home of your Hijrah; full of date palms, between two stony lands (harrah). So those who were to go made Hijrah toward Madinah; and most of those who had made Hijrah to Abyssinia also returned to Madinah.{{2}}
blocks.79: Then from Makkah, on the road to Madinah, people began to leave one or two at a time. Who arrived first, al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) has told.
blocks.81: The first to come to us were Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum (RA); they would teach the people the Qur’an. Then came Bilal, Sa‘d and ‘Ammar ibn Yasir (RA). Then ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) came with twenty of the Companions of the Prophet {{1}}. Then the Prophet {{2}} came. I never saw the people of Madinah as happy about anything as they were at the arrival of the Messenger of Allah {{3}}. Even the slave girls were saying, the Messenger of Allah {{4}} has come! Before he came I had already recited several surahs of the Mufassal, including ‘Sabbih isma Rabbika al-A‘la’.{{5}}
blocks.82: Madinah was filling up. But not everyone’s road was easy. The Prophet {{1}} used to tell the travellers one thing; Allah has arranged for you brothers and a home where you will be safe.{{2}}
blocks.84: Among the Muhajirun of Makkah, the first to set out on the road to Madinah was Abu Salamah (RA). About a year before the pledge of ‘Aqabah.{{1}}
blocks.85: He seated his wife Umm Salamah (RA) and their infant son Salamah on the camel. He himself took the reins. Umm Salamah (RA) later told in her own words what happened.
blocks.86: When Abu Salamah (RA) set out leading me by the camel’s reins, the men of Banu Mughirah stood before him. They said, you have been lost to us as regards yourself. But on what assurance will you take this daughter of ours around from town to town? They snatched the reins from his hand and tore me away. Then Banu ‘Abd al-Asad, the tribe of Abu Salamah (RA), grew angry. They said, by Allah, we will not leave our boy with her. They pulled at my son Salamah until even his hand was dislocated. Then Banu ‘Abd al-Asad took him away, and Banu Mughirah kept me back. Abu Salamah (RA) went on to Madinah. Between me and my son and husband a separation came.{{1}}
blocks.87: Every morning I would go out and sit at al-Abtah. I would weep until evening. So for a year, or close to it.{{1}}
blocks.88: One day a cousin from Banu Mughirah was passing that way. Pity came over him. He said to the tribesmen, why are you not letting this helpless girl go? You separated her from her husband, and from her son too. They said, go, go to your husband, if you wish. Banu ‘Abd al-Asad also gave the boy back. Umm Salamah (RA) set out on a camel, seating her son on her lap. No one else with her. Only Allah, and the boy. At a place named Tan‘im she met ‘Uthman ibn Talhah. He was still a polytheist. He asked, where are you going? Umm Salamah (RA) said, to Madinah, to my husband. He said, no one is with you? The answer came, no one but Allah and this boy. ‘Uthman ibn Talhah said, by Allah, you cannot be left alone. He took the camel’s reins and walked.
blocks.89: By Allah, I never found a gentler companion than him among any man of the Arabs. Wherever we stopped, he would make the camel kneel and step aside. When I got down, he would unload the camel and tie it to a tree, then go away and lie down under a tree. When it was time to set out, he would bring the camel forward, saddle it, and step back, saying, mount. When I had settled properly, he would come and take the reins. In this way he brought me to Madinah. When the settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf at Quba came into view, he said, your husband is in that village. Enter with Allah’s blessing. Then he turned back toward Makkah.{{1}}
blocks.90: Umm Salamah (RA) would later say, no household in Islam suffered such hardship as the family of Abu Salamah (RA).

In Ibn Ishaq’s account the names of the six: As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA), ‘Awf ibn al-Harith (RA), Rafi‘ ibn Malik (RA), Qutbah ibn ‘Amir (RA), ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Amir (RA), Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah ibn Ri’ab (RA). In it is also the statement of ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA): we were at the first ‘Aqabah, twelve; we pledged like the pledge of the women, before war was made obligatory.

A narration of the Sirah, as a scene.

Source: Musnad Ahmad 15798 (Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: ‘qawi’, that is, strong; al-Haythami: the narrators of Ahmad are narrators of the Sahih, except Ibn Ishaq, and he has stated direct hearing); Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’. He is the father of Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA). In one narration of Bukhari, Jabir (RA) himself also said, I, my father and my two maternal uncles were at ‘Aqabah (Ibn Kathir has quoted it).
footnotes.14: Numbers: in the narration of Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA), seventy-three men and two women (Ibn Ishaq; al-Bidayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’). In the narration of ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, seventy men and one woman; Ibn Kathir wrote that the Arabs are accustomed to stating numbers leaving out fractions. In the hadith of Jabir (RA) too, ‘seventy’ has come (Musnad Ahmad 14456).
footnotes.15: The speech of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib (summarised in meaning): Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’ (the narration of Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA), via Ibn Ishaq; from the Sirah). ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib had not believed at this time; he believed later.

footnotes.17: Musnad Ahmad 14456 (from Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA)); Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: chain sahih

footnotes.19: The question of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA) and the Prophet’s {{1}} answer: Musnad Ahmad 15798 (from Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA); via Ibn Ishaq). The answer’s sentence ‘bal ad-dama ad-dama, wal-hadma al-hadma’ is proverb-like Arabic; its meaning: your blood is my blood, your ruin is my ruin. A narration of the Sirah.

In Ibn Ishaq’s list the nine of the Khazraj: As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA), Sa‘d ibn al-Rabi‘ (RA), ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA), Rafi‘ ibn Malik (RA), al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur (RA), ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA), ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA), Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA), Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA); the three of the Aws: Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA), Sa‘d ibn Khaythamah (RA), Rifa‘ah ibn ‘Abd al-Mundhir (RA) (in the view of Ibn Hisham, in place of Rifa‘ah, Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA)). This difference in the list Ibn Kathir himself mentions.

footnotes.23: The shout on the night of ‘Aqabah, the proposal of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) and the coming of the elders of Quraysh the next morning: Musnad Ahmad 15798 (from Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA); via Ibn Ishaq). The word ‘Mudhammam’ (the condemned) used in Shaytan’s call: the Quraysh used to say this mockingly instead of calling the Prophet {{1}} ‘Muhammad’ (the praised); the explanation of Ibn Ishaq, the narrator in the Musnad: ‘the enemy of Allah was saying Muhammad’. A narration of the Sirah.
footnotes.24: The shoes incident: Musnad Ahmad 15798 (from Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA); via Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah). In this narration the name of the Qurayshi youth is al-Harith ibn Hisham al-Makhzumi; he believed later.
footnotes.25: Quraysh’s going to ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his denial: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’ (Ibn Ishaq, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene).
footnotes.26: Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah’s (RA) own account: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’ (via Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene)
footnotes.27: The freeing of Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (from Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene). In Ibn Hisham’s different account, the name of the man who punched him is Suhayl ibn ‘Amr, and the name of the man who suggested calling them is Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham. For the two who freed him, Ibn Kathir wrote ‘Jubayr ibn Mut‘im’ and ‘al-Harith ibn Harb’. The same incident is also in al-Raheeq al-Makhtum (Allamah Safiur Rahman Mubarakpuri, p. 272; citing Ibn Hisham and Zad al-Ma‘ad as sources).
footnotes.28: The description of the home seen in the dream: al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 5706 (from Suhayb (RA)): ‘Uritu dara hijratikum sabkhatan bayna zahrani harratin, fa-imma an takuna Hajaran aw takuna Yathriba’; al-Hakim: chain sahih, al-Dhahabi: sahih. In this narration doubt about the name of the place is reported.
footnotes.31: The command of Hijrah and the Prophet’s {{1}} words: Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Chapter on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah’ (from Ibn Ishaq): ‘Innallaha qad ja‘ala lakum ikhwanan wa daran ta’manuna biha’. A narration of the Sirah, as a scene.
footnotes.32: The first Hijrah of Abu Salamah (RA) and the story of Umm Salamah (RA): Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Chapter on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah’ (Ibn Ishaq ← his father Yasar ← Salamah ibn ‘Abdillah ← his grandmother Umm Salamah (RA)). The account from the witness’s own mouth, with connected chain; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene. It is also in al-Raheeq al-Makhtum, pp. 273–274.
footnotes.33: From Umm Salamah (RA): Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Chapter on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah’ (via Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene)
footnotes.34: From Umm Salamah (RA): Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Chapter on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah’ (via Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene)
footnotes.35: From Umm Salamah (RA): Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, ‘Chapter on the Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah’ (via Ibn Ishaq; a narration of the Sirah, as a scene); Ibn Kathir wrote that ‘Uthman ibn Talhah believed after Hudaybiyah

quiz.q: In the narration of Ibn ‘Abbas (RA), how many years did the Prophet ﷺ stay in Makkah after receiving prophethood?
o: Thirteen years
Ten years, as long as he went around calling at the markets
Fourteen nights, as long as he stayed at Quba
Three nights, as long as he hid in the cave of Thawr
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3902 and 3851: for thirteen years in Makkah revelation came; then the command of Hijrah.

quiz.q: Someone does not calculate in business, saying ‘Allah is my trust’. With which scene of the Hijrah can he be made to understand?
o: Sitting only three nights in the cave, with the spider’s web, and getting results with no arrangement at all
After four months of preparation and a guide, saying in the cave ‘Allah is with us’
Suhayb (RA) gaining release by giving gold, where the arrangement was only the giving of gold
Building a mosque where the she-camel knelt, where no price had to be paid
quiz.e: The answer to today’s question: trust and calculation together.

quiz.q: In the narration of Jabir ibn ‘Abdillah (RA), at which places did the Prophet ﷺ go to the people in search of a home?
o: The pass of ‘Aqabah, the cave of Thawr and Quba
‘Ukaz and Majinnah, and in the Hajj season at Mina
The harrah, the settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf and the date-drying yard of the mosque
The settlement of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf and the courtyard of Abu Ayyub (RA)

quiz.q: In the Hajj season the Prophet ﷺ would say, ‘Who will give me shelter? Who will help me?’ What was the promise in return?
o: A reward equal to the blood-price, which Quraysh had announced
A written paper of security, which was written for Suraqah
Paradise
The glad tidings of a ‘profitable trade’, which were given to Suhayb (RA)

quiz.q: What is said about the day of Bu‘ath in the narration of ‘A’ishah (RA)?
o: On that day the Prophet ﷺ came to the house of Abu Bakr (RA) at the harsh time of noon
On that day al-Zubayr (RA) met the Muslim caravan returning from Syria
On that day seventy-three men gathered in the pass of ‘Aqabah
Allah had brought that day forward for His Messenger

quiz.q: How did the war of Bu‘ath make easier the way for Islam to come?
o: The Jews had promised to protect the Muslims, in this hope
Quraysh had stopped looking toward Madinah, in this hope
With the tribes’ ranks broken and the chiefs killed, the way became easier
‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib had made a pact with Yathrib, in this hope
quiz.e: According to the narration of ‘A’ishah (RA) (Sahih al-Bukhari 3777).

quiz.q: According to Ibn Ishaq’s narration, to which tribe did the first six who met the Prophet ﷺ belong?
o: Khazraj
Aws, with whom the Khazraj used to fight
Quraysh, who lived in Makkah
Banu Dil, one of whom became a guide

quiz.q: Why did the six not delay in believing?
o: Hearing the promise of Paradise in the terms of ‘Aqabah, which was an event of the second ‘Aqabah
Thinking, this is the very prophet the Jews threatened them with
Hearing the warning of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib, which was an event of the second ‘Aqabah
Seeing the sign of the she-camel kneeling, which happened in Madinah
quiz.e: The words of the six: this is the very prophet; let them not reach him before us (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: How many came at the first ‘Aqabah pledge?
o: Seventy-three, who were at the second ‘Aqabah
Six, who were at the first meeting
Twelve
Seventy, the number in the hadith of Jabir (RA)
quiz.e: Ten of the Khazraj and two of the Aws (Ibn Ishaq).

quiz.q: Which is the term of the pledge narrated by ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA)?
o: Choosing twelve naqibs and taking responsibility for the tribes, which happened at the second ‘Aqabah
Protecting me as you protect your wives and children, which was a term of the second ‘Aqabah
Whoever you make peace with, I will make peace with, which was said to Abu al-Haytham
Abstaining from shirk, theft, adultery, unjust killing and plunder

quiz.q: According to Ibn Ishaq’s account, the pledge of the first ‘Aqabah was from what time?
o: After hiding in the cave of Thawr
The time of staying fourteen nights at Quba
After Suraqah went back
Before war was made obligatory
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq: like the pledge of the women, before war was made obligatory (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: In the narration of Jabir (RA), how did Islam spread in Yathrib?
o: Hearing of the Jews’ threats, all the tribes believed together
One would believe and, having learned the Qur’an, return, and his people too would become Muslims
After the war of Bu‘ath the tribes united, then everyone believed
Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) came and in a single day called everyone and made them Muslims

quiz.q: What lesson does the dars attach to Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr’s (RA) going to Madinah?
o: The ground was prepared by a teacher, not an army
Gathering in the dark of the night at the pass of ‘Aqabah was the real work
Going back, unable to catch him, was Suraqah’s real victory
The kneeling of the she-camel was the real preparation
quiz.e: Mus‘ab (RA) went first; then the Prophet ﷺ; by then the home was ready.

quiz.q: Your child wants to learn the din from someone. What can be learned from the story of Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) in Madinah?
o: Only the preparation of swords is the real thing
To teach everything oneself, without sending a teacher
A capable teacher builds the home
A secret caravan is needed to teach the din

quiz.q: In the narration of Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA), how many men and how many women were there on the night of the second ‘Aqabah?
o: Twelve men and two women, the number of the first ‘Aqabah
Seventy men and one woman, the narration of ‘Urwah
Seventy-three men and two women
Six men, no woman, the number of the first meeting
quiz.e: In the narration of ‘Urwah and Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, seventy and one (Ibn Kathir).

quiz.q: Who were the two women Companions present at the second ‘Aqabah?
o: ‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr (RA) and Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (RA)
Asma’ bint Abi Bakr (RA) and Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA)
Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA) and ‘A’ishah bint Abi Bakr (RA)
Nusaybah bint Ka‘b (RA) and Asma’ bint ‘Amr (RA)
quiz.e: Al-Bidayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’.

quiz.q: Who spoke first of all on the night of ‘Aqabah?
o: His uncle ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib
The youngest, As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA)
The chief al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur (RA), who first took his hand
Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA), who raised the question of the pact
quiz.e: First of all, the word of his uncle ‘Abbas (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: Your friend has known the truth for many years and still does not believe. What can be learned from the story of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr ibn Haram (RA)?
o: No need to speak once the friend understands by himself; he will come on his own
It is enough to make the friend memorise the terms of ‘Aqabah; the rest is his work
Winning an argument in front of Quraysh, silencing him and turning him back
Speaking with love: ‘You will be fuel for Hell; I cannot accept it’
quiz.e: Al-Bidayah, ‘Story of the second pledge of ‘Aqabah’.

quiz.q: What did As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA) warn of before the pledge?
o: We are cutting the old pacts; will the Prophet ﷺ go back? (the question of Abu al-Haytham)
Taking the Prophet ﷺ out means a break with all of Arabia
Tomorrow we will fall upon the people of Mina with our swords (the proposal of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA))
We are children of war, we inherited arms (the words of al-Bara’ (RA))

quiz.q: In answer to the question of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: I have not been commanded to do this, which was said to ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA)
What do you think of two of whom the third is Allah? which was said to Abu Bakr (RA)
I am yours, you are mine
In exchange for a price, which was said when taking Abu Bakr’s (RA) mount

quiz.q: At the second ‘Aqabah, what were the number and division of the naqibs the Prophet ﷺ asked for?
o: Twelve; ten of the Khazraj, two of the Aws
Six; all of the Khazraj
Seventy-three; among them two women
Twelve; nine of the Khazraj, three of the Aws

quiz.q: What is understood from the warning of As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA)?
o: The pledge was kept hidden because no one was willing to take the risk
The risk was told openly to everyone before the pledge
The Prophet ﷺ himself objected to taking the pledge
Quraysh already knew all the terms of the pledge

quiz.q: Hearing the shout from ‘Aqabah, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: This is the ‘Azab of ‘Aqabah, the son of Azyab; I will make time for you
Mount in safety and be followed, which the Ansar said at the harrah
Keep our matter secret, which was said to Suraqah
Go slowly; I hope I will be permitted too, which was said to Abu Bakr (RA)

quiz.q: What did ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) propose to the Prophet ﷺ?
o: To deny everything by oath before Quraysh, like the polytheists of the caravan
To fall upon the people of Mina with swords the very next day
To take one of two mounts, like Abu Bakr (RA)
To donate the yard, like the two boys
quiz.e: Answer: ‘I have not been commanded to do this’ (Musnad Ahmad 15798).

quiz.q: What did Ka‘b ibn Malik (RA) say about the oath of the polytheists of the caravan?
o: They swore falsely, pretending though they knew everything
They spoke out of fear of the Muslims, though they knew the real matter
They spoke the truth; they did not know
They spoke on the order of ‘Abbas ibn ‘Ubadah (RA), knowing it

quiz.q: Which naqib was caught by Quraysh after ‘Aqabah?
o: Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA), who broke away and escaped
Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA)
As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA), who had stopped them before the pledge
Al-Bara’ ibn Ma‘rur (RA), who first took his hand

quiz.q: How was Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA) released?
o: By agreeing to give gold, like Suhayb (RA)
By changing beds, like ‘Ali (RA)
By mentioning the security he had given to two merchants of Quraysh
Through the intercession of ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy
quiz.e: By calling out the names of Jubayr ibn Mut‘im and al-Harith ibn Harb (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: A trader does not value small good conduct. What can be said from the story of Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah (RA)?
o: By conduct, people’s loyalty can be bought
An opportunity is created for the enemy to ask forgiveness
The profit of business only keeps increasing
In the future it can save life in danger
quiz.e: The two merchants to whom he had given security were the ones who freed him.

quiz.q: Who first came to Madinah and began to teach people the Qur’an?
o: Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr (RA) and Ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
Bilal (RA) and ‘Ammar ibn Yasir (RA), who came after
‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and the twenty with him
As‘ad ibn Zurarah (RA) and ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA), who were people of Madinah itself

quiz.q: Which statement did al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) make about himself?
o: He held a cloth and shaded the Prophet ﷺ from the sun at Quba, which was the act of Abu Bakr (RA)
Before the Prophet ﷺ came he had already recited several surahs of the Mufassal
He held his hand and stopped everyone before the pledge, which was the act of As‘ad (RA)
He slept in the Prophet’s ﷺ bed that night, which was the act of ‘Ali (RA)

quiz.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ see the home of the Hijrah in the dream (Sahih al-Bukhari 3905)?
o: At the foot of Mount Thawr, between two caves
Beside a high fortress, in the Jewish settlement
Full of date palms, between two harrahs
Beside the pass of ‘Aqabah, within the tents of Mina

quiz.q: Who escorted Umm Salamah (RA) on the road to Madinah?
o: Abu Salamah (RA), who had reached Madinah earlier
‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, who brought news to the cave
‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), who grazed the sheep
‘Uthman ibn Talhah, still a polytheist
quiz.e: Met at Tan‘im; up to Quba (al-Bidayah).

quiz.q: Someone finds it hard to walk the path of din under family pressure. What can be learned from the story of Umm Salamah (RA)?
o: Leaving a business when it makes a loss, for the same reason
Trusting without opening the books before an exam, for the same reason
Bearing separation and weeping with patience, the way opens
Leaving a trust with someone, for the same reason
